questions.knowledge_point: Finding a Quartic Polynomial Given Four Real Roots
questions.problem: The quartic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=2,$ and ${x}_{4}=-1$ and the coefficient of the quartic term is $1.$ Find $P(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
Since our quartic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=2,$ and ${x}_{4}=-1,$ and the coefficient of the quartic term is $a=1,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3})(x-{x}_{4}) & =1(x-2)(x-2)(x-2)(x-(-1)) \\  & =1(x-2)(x-2)(x-2)(x+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}1(x-2)(x-2)(x-2)(x+1) & =1({x}^{2}-4x+4)({x}^{2}-x-2) \\  & =1({x}^{4}-{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-4{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}+8x+4{x}^{2}-4x-8) \\  & =1({x}^{4}-5{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}+4x-8) \\  & ={x}^{4}-5{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}+4x-8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)={x}^{4}-5{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}+4x-8.$

questions.problem:
The quartic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=3,$ and ${x}_{4}=-4$ and the coefficient of the quartic term is $1.$ Determine the **expanded form** of $P(x).$

$P(x)=$

$-\,108$
questions.worked_solution:
Since our quartic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=3,$ and ${x}_{4}=-4,$ and the coefficient of the quartic term is $a=1,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3})(x-{x}_{4}) & =1(x-3)(x-3)(x-3)(x-(-4)) \\  & =(x-3)(x-3)(x-3)(x+4)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-3)(x-3)(x-3)(x+4) & =({x}^{2}-6x+9)({x}^{2}+x-12) \\  & ={x}^{4}+{x}^{3}-12{x}^{2}-6{x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}+72x+9{x}^{2}+9x-108 \\  & ={x}^{4}-5{x}^{3}-9{x}^{2}+81x-108.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)={x}^{4}-5{x}^{3}-9{x}^{2}+81x-108.$

The Argand diagram above shows the roots of a quartic polynomial $f(x).$ Determine the **expanded form** of $f(x)$ given that the coefficient of the quartic term is $2.$

$f(x)=$
{{field-1}}
$+\,72$
questions.worked_solution:
From the diagram, we see that $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1,2}=\pm \text{i}$ and ${x}_{3,4}=\pm 6\text{i}.$ Additionally, we're given that the coefficient of the quartic term is $a=2.$ Therefore, we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3})(x-{x}_{4}) \\  & =2(x-(-\text{i}))(x-\text{i})(x-(-6\text{i}))(x-6\text{i}) \\  & =2(x+\text{i})(x-\text{i})(x+6\text{i})(x-6\text{i})\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2(x+\text{i})(x-\text{i})(x+6\text{i})(x-6\text{i}) & = \\ 2({x}^{2}+(\text{i}-\text{i})x-{\text{i}}^{2})({x}^{2}+(6\text{i}-6\text{i})x-36{\text{i}}^{2}) & = \\ 2({x}^{2}+1)({x}^{2}+36) & = \\ 2({x}^{4}+36{x}^{2}+{x}^{2}+36) & = \\ 2({x}^{4}+37{x}^{2}+36) & = \\ 2{x}^{4}+74{x}^{2}+72 & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=2{x}^{4}+74{x}^{2}+72.$

questions.worked_solution:
From the diagram, we see that $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1,2}=-2\pm 3\text{i},$ and ${x}_{3,4}=1\pm \text{i}.$ Additionally, we're given that the coefficient of the quartic term is $a=2.$ Therefore, we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3})(x-{x}_{4}) \\  & =2(x-(-2+3\text{i}))(x-(-2-3\text{i}))(x-(1+\text{i}))(x-(1-\text{i}))\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2(x-(-2+3\text{i}))(x-(-2-3\text{i}))(x-(1+\text{i}))(x-(1-\text{i})) & = \\ 2({x}^{2}+4x+4+9)({x}^{2}-2x+1+1) & = \\ 2({x}^{2}+4x+13)({x}^{2}-2x+2) & = \\ 2({x}^{4}-2{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}+4{x}^{3}-8{x}^{2}+8x+13{x}^{2}-26x+26) & = \\ 2({x}^{4}+2{x}^{3}+7{x}^{2}-18x+26) & = \\ 2{x}^{4}+4{x}^{3}+14{x}^{2}-36x+52 & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=2{x}^{4}+4{x}^{3}+14{x}^{2}-36x+52.$

questions.worked_solution:
From the diagram, we see that $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-3,$ ${x}_{2}=2,$ and ${x}_{3,4}=-1\pm \text{i}.$ Additionally, we're given that the coefficient of the quartic term is $a=3.$ Therefore, we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3})(x-{x}_{4}) \\  & =3(x-(-3))(x-2)(x-(-1+\text{i}))(x-(-1-\text{i})) \\  & =3(x+3)(x-2)(x-(-1+\text{i}))(x-(-1-\text{i}))\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}3(x+3)(x-2)(x-(-1+\text{i}))(x-(-1-\text{i})) & = \\ 3({x}^{2}-2x+3x-6)({x}^{2}-x(-1-\text{i})-x(-1+\text{i})+(-1+\text{i})(-1-\text{i})) & = \\ 3({x}^{2}+x-6)\,({x}^{2}+2x+2) & = \\ 3({x}^{4}+2{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}+{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}+2x-6{x}^{2}-12x-12) & = \\ 3({x}^{4}+3{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-10x-12) & = \\ 3{x}^{4}+9{x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}-30x-36 & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=3{x}^{4}+9{x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}-30x-36.$
